correctness.rationale: Multiplicativity reduces the valuation to local factors. In the root case, Dirichlet's theorem supplies a prime set with divergent reciprocal sum; the events that each such prime divides n exactly once have independent natural densities, so their count tends to infinity in density. In the non-root case, no exponent-one local factor contributes, and the mean is bounded by the displayed convergent series over repeated prime powers. The cyclic-group solvability criterion gives the stated two-adic boundary.

value.rationale: The result classifies a natural valuation invariant for every fixed prime p and power-sum exponent r. The boundary is structural: the existence of an r-th root of -1 modulo p determines whether exponent-one prime factors force unbounded valuation in density; otherwise repeated prime powers contribute only a uniformly bounded mean. This gives both a complete dichotomy and a useful obstruction for studying divisibility of generalized divisor sums.
